name: Camille Galliard-Minier
bio: Camille Galliard-Minier (née Galliard) is a French politician and lawyer, born 26 May 1975 in La Tronche (Isère). She earned a doctorate in law in 2003 (thesis on simple and full adoption, supervised by Pierre Murat) and practised as a lawyer at the Grenoble bar from 2003 until 2017, specialising notably in family law and criminal law. She comes from a family active in local politics: her grandfather Louis Gaillard was mayor of La Tronche (1971-1985). A member of the centre-left and of La République En Marche / Renaissance, she was Olivier Véran's substitute in Isère's 1st constituency at the 2017 legislative elections and became deputy in March 2020 when Véran was appointed Minister of Health, serving until 2022. She did not stand in the 2022 election. In 2022 she founded the Grenoble-based endowment fund Sesame, which connects local businesses with solidarity associations. She was re-elected deputy for Isère's 1st constituency in a January 2025 by-election (Ensemble pour la République). On 26 February 2026 she was appointed Minister-Delegate for Autonomy and Disabled Persons in Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's government, reporting to the Minister of Health, Families, Autonomy and Disabled Persons (Stéphanie Rist).
